corridor_notes: Project name confirmed as '溧高管道工程' (Liyang-Gaochun pipeline project), part of '川气东送江苏配套管线一期工程' (Sichuan-East Jiangsu supporting pipeline phase 1) -- an EIA report with this exact title is catalogued on doc88.com (57pp PDF, uploaded 2014-12-26, paywalled, no free preview text). A Jiangsu provincial government land-use approval, '江苏省人民政府关于川气东送管道高淳分输站项目建设用地的批复' (苏政地[2015]24号, dated ~2015-04-09), confirms a '高淳分输站' (Gaochun distribution station) was built for this project, but the specific town/village within Gaochun District was not recoverable -- the hosting pages (lawlawing.com, wenku.baidu.com) were unreachable/blocked. A Pengpai/thepaper.cn retrospective article ('辉煌十年·看高淳') stated Gaochun connected to the Sichuan-East pipeline from Liyang in 2013 and began formal gas utilization in 2015, corroborating the general Liyang-to-Gaochun corridor and timeline, but that article has since been deleted (404 on both the desktop and mobile URLs, confirmed via direct fetch and via the r.jina.ai reader proxy) so it cannot serve as a citable ref.
researcher_notes: Corridor (Liyang -> Gaochun district) and project identity are well corroborated by multiple independent snippets, but no accessible source gave a station/township-level place name for either end that I could geocode and cite. No coordinates invented per standing instructions. A human with access to a paid doc88/docin account, or Jiangsu/Nanjing government EIA archives, could likely resolve this quickly -- the underlying documents clearly exist (EIA report + provincial land-use approval), they are just paywalled or unreachable through this session's tools.
blockers: No verifiable ref with station-level place names was found. Candidate documents identified but inaccessible: doc88.com/p-3127535294710.html (paywalled, generic metadata only, failed content check), lawlawing.com/community/157137 (ECONNREFUSED), wenku.baidu.com/view/24fe5e7ae618964bcf84b9d528ea81c758f52e02.html (HTTP 403), thepaper.cn article (deleted/404). WebSearch tool budget was exhausted (200/200) mid-session; remaining searches relied on DuckDuckGo (frequent CAPTCHA) and Sogou (frequent anti-spider block) via WebFetch, and archive.org's availability API was repeatedly rate-limited (429), likely from concurrent sibling research agents in this same batch hitting it simultaneously -- a retry with a clean web-search budget and without archive.org contention would likely resolve this PID.
